name: Taiwan (TSMC)
summary: Taiwan, Day 266. TAIEX fell 6.23% to 36,033.29 on 20 Nov after −4.4% the day before — −17.5% on the week, Bloomberg's worst week since 1991 — as the US AI/chip rout (the AMD short report, Anthropic's IPO 'sell the news') met a direct hit to Taiwan's champions: new US rules closing a manufacturing loophole, with TSMC tightening China AI-chip curbs and pausing some shipments. TSMC is −15% on the week. Friday's fall was driven more by local dealer hedging than by foreign selling, which eased after Thursday's NT$76.6bn. It is not a record day (−6.03% on 16 Nov). There is no helium- or gas-driven production change and no war link (~0%). The war reaches Taiwan through the AI financing cycle, US rates and export policy, not supply. Watch: TSMC helium/gas allocation change — not fired.

recent_signals.headline: TAIEX -6.5% Friday, -6.8% on the month but still +15.9% on three months. **The tell of the whole Asian tech move: TSMC posted a blowout quarter — net profit +77%, capex raised to $60-64bn — and was SOLD anyway.** That is a valuation unwind, not a war trade. Taiwan's genuine crisis exposure is helium at **~69% GCC dependence** (higher than commonly reported), against ~30-35% of global supply offline for 3-5 years; TSMC says it expects no significant near-term impact, citing diversified contracts and on-site recycling capex the Korean memory fabs lack. CONFIRMED.
